findings.evidence: Both handlers only caught SessionResolutionException/ApiException, so an unexpected exception (e.g. a JSON-parse TypeError/FormatException from a malformed server response) would propagate uncaught, leaving the bloc permanently stuck in AttemptStarting with no route to AttemptError.
findings.why_it_matters: Mirrors the exact failure mode Phase 1's AuthBloc already had to fix (QUAL-103): the user is left on a permanently-spinning, permanently-disabled entry screen with no recoverable state.
findings.required_action: Widen the catch to a catch-all mapping unexpected exceptions to AttemptError, matching AuthBloc's established pattern.
findings.resolution: Both handlers now use a broad catch (e) and a new _asAttemptException(Object error) helper (error is Exception ? error : UnknownApiException(error.toString())) before emitting AttemptError. Verified via a new test throwing FormatException from startOrResumeAttempt and asserting [AttemptStarting, AttemptError].

findings.evidence: Resume reconciliation called SyncEngine.startSync whenever !response.completed, before _emitFromResponse separately re-checked response.task for null. A contract-violating completed:false/task:null response would arm SyncEngine for that attempt, then _emitFromResponse would emit AttemptError without ever calling stopSync(), orphaning a running background sync session.
findings.why_it_matters: Per SyncEngine.startSync's own contract, the next legitimate startSync call for a different attempt would throw StateError, crashing a subsequent attempt start over an edge-case malformed response.
findings.required_action: Call stopSync() before emitting AttemptError in this branch, or move the startSync/flushNow call after the task==null check succeeds.
findings.resolution: The reconciliation guard is now `if (!response.completed && response.task != null)`, matching _emitFromResponse's own null-task check, so startSync/flushNow are never called for that contract-violating shape in the first place. Verified via a new test confirming completed:false/task:null produces AttemptError with syncEngine.startSync/flushNow never called. Confirmed _onNextTaskRequested has no equivalent risk (it never calls startSync).

findings.evidence: SnackBar(content: Text(state.error.toString())) renders the internal exception class name (e.g. "ValidationException: Session ID cannot be empty.") directly to the user.
findings.why_it_matters: Not a localizable, user-appropriate message — placeholder-quality UX, acceptable for this phase's scope.
findings.required_action: Not required to unblock this gate. Consider mapping AttemptError.error to a user-facing string when a message layer exists.
